title: Combine AI’s
author: Puzzleheaded-Plenty1
selftext:
How much if any benefit would it be to use multiple AI in game development?

Currently I have GPT doing the game for everything. Would, at times having another AI do work in the game be more or less beneficial?

Or would they just circle of death themselves?

comments.author: olafthemanofsnow
comments.body: Build a work flow so you can map out what you need for each thing. I use multiple AI tools to help with different things depending on what needs doing at the time.

comments.author: snobesque
comments.body: Claude is really much better in coding than chat gpt. This is quite a good reason to use it as well

replies.author: eduardopy
replies.body: Eh not really, maybe in some edge cases but for game dev its whatever.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body: For game dev opus 5.5 is the best option for the money

replies.author: eduardopy
replies.body: Yeah thats what the hivemind decided for this week. I think people get too hung up on what others think.

replies.author: ChadSexman
replies.body:
The “hivemind” is basing their information off scientific benchmarking that is updated daily.

For complex coding work, Opus 5.5 offers the best bang for your buck, for now.

I would love to see your data that suggests otherwise, but I get the impression you’re more interested in being a contrarian.

replies.author: eduardopy
replies.body: Yeah thats my point, we are in the game dev sub no? At this point most models are fine for it. Yeah im a contrarian I wont deny it but I have been around for a long time and seen how the “ai community“ changes their opinion faster than its members change their underwear. Personally? Ive been having different experiences than those parrotted here which is why im a bit of a contrarian. Really im just pro rationality.

comments.author: SubzeroSun
comments.body: Use another for review; might catch something that was missed entirely.

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
comments.body:
You can try a small two-role test before handing both models the whole project: let GPT implement one change, then give the other model the same requirements and the diff and ask it to identify specific failure cases without editing files. For example, if you add pause/resume, check in the running game whether movement and timers stop and restart as intended.



Keep one short note with the engine version and current rules, and have only one writer change a file at a time. That makes it less likely they’ll undo each other. Two models can agree on the same mistake, so test their suggestions rather than treating agreement as proof. If the extra review doesn’t catch anything useful, it may not be worth the time and cost for that task.

comments.author: daddy_reloaded
comments.body:
Different ai tool doing different tasks yes.
Different ai doing the same kind of tasks no. 
Few exceptions for art stuff.

comments.author: shuozhe
comments.body: Install all the cli tool on the same agent.. "let agy carbon do a review" using that a lot recently

comments.author: Enderoth
comments.body: I use Claude for code, ChatGPT for some image generation, and PixelLab for in game art, music, and foley/sfx. All have their place.

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
Using different AI is like using different people.

It's powerful to bounce ideas back and forth. Diversity of ideas is a good thing.

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: the circle of death mostly happens when two models keep editing the same files and each rewrites the other's choices. keep one model as the only one that writes code and use the second only for reading. paste the code and ask what would break, then you decide what goes back to the writer. the code stays one style and you still get the second opinion

comments.author: nanotyrannusgames
comments.body: I use Claude for the code, GPT for the art.

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: Usually it helps more as a review step than as a parallel builder. A lot of devs have one model write the feature and then paste the diff into a different one to ask what could break, since a second model often catches mistakes the first one keeps repeating. The circle of death mostly happens when two models both edit the same files with no shared context. Worth trying one source of truth, like a short design doc or notes file that every model reads, and keeping each model on its own task (code, art prompts, balancing numbers).

comments.author: Arcodiant
comments.body: You'll benefit from using different models and providers to cross-check each other, especially when it comes to reviews - asking Claude to review Claude's code will retain the same biases, but having GPT review Claude's code will give you better feedback
